subject: physics
question_text: Distinguish between a scalar and a vector. Give one example of each.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Scalar
lines: A scalar has magnitude only. A number
with its unit describes it completely,
and scalars add by ordinary arithmetic.
steps.why: The real test is not "does it point somewhere in the picture" but "do I need a direction to add two of them correctly".
common_mistakes: Calling speed a vector — speed is the size of velocity and carries no direction.

recall.must_convey: That a scalar has magnitude only and adds by ordinary arithmetic.
accept: just a number and a unit

steps.label: Vector
lines: A vector has both magnitude and direction,
and it adds by the triangle or the
steps.why: The addition law is the working definition: 3 N and 4 N can give 5 N, which no pair of scalars ever does.
common_mistakes: Saying only "it has direction" — the mark scheme also requires the addition law.

recall.must_convey: That a vector has magnitude and direction and adds by the triangle or parallelogram law.
